terminologyReview: Guideline clarification: the revised distinction in references/common.md and references/ga.md is correct. The evidence agrees on three points. intl-workerd.json shows Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat unsupported (English output) for eo, be and ga, while Intl.PluralRules returns native categories for all 18 locales. InstructionTemplates (packages/shared/src/instruction-template.ts) builds Intl.PluralRules for the content language and throws when a catalog omits a native count variant or a message. BotText.andList and transcriptLabelList join items only through the catalog's formatting.* patterns. So Bickr's own formatters never 'silently return English'; the English fallback is only a property of the platform Intl list and relative-time formatters, which Bickr does not use for these strings. One leftover: references/eo.md line 7 still says 'The runtime formatters silently return English, although plural rules work.' It should use the same wording as common.md and ga.md (be.md already does). This is a guideline edit only and changes no frozen English unit.

German terminology follows the lead decisions. Kennung takes feminine articles everywhere (system.identity fixed; no other mismatch found by an article scan). "Codeblock mit Begrenzungszeilen" is the only fenced-block term (no "eingezäunt" left). "Entfolgen" is used in the tool description, with explanatory "nicht mehr folgen" in schema fields. "Darf nicht leer sein" is used for mandatory non-empty fields. The generic nouns Teilnehmer and teilnehmende Person do not attribute a gender to the first-person speaker. Sie imperatives and ich narration are consistent.

Modal force: "darf höchstens" for the Mermaid size limit and "muss höchstens … sein" for character limits both express a binding maximum. That is consistent with the source "must be at most", and the de.md rule (dürfen nicht for a permission ban) does not make "darf höchstens" a weaker statement.

opus.reason: Adopts my optional coordination fix ("mit Begrenzungszeilen und der Kennzeichnung svg"). The lead also rewrites the Mermaid limit as "Begrenzen Sie den Mermaid-Quelltext auf höchstens {{mermaidKiB}} KiB." That is a binding imperative with the same maximum, and it matches the SVG and math sentences ("Begrenzen Sie … auf"). I agree with the lead that "darf höchstens" was not a weaker permission, so Grok's required change was unnecessary. The imperative removes the dispute without copying an English modal. grok.reason: Accept Begrenzen Sie den Mermaid-Quelltext auf höchstens {{mermaidKiB}} KiB. English requires that maximum. The imperative states it directly, in the same pattern as the SVG bound, without copying must onto muss. It is not a permission to exceed the size. muss nicht lang sein still means a reply does not need to be long. The svg label is now coordinated with und, so the second mit no longer attaches to the fence. The element, viewBox, feature bans, and element limit stay.

opus.reason: The fenced-block alignment is right. On Grok's proposal I agree with the lead's choice not to adopt it. One optional point, caused by my own comparison-stage edit: the SVG sentence now reads "in einem Codeblock mit Begrenzungszeilen mit der Kennzeichnung svg", with "mit" twice. The Mermaid sentence has "mit Begrenzungszeilen und der Kennzeichnung mermaid", so use the same coordination.

The imperative states the same rule clearly without a literal modal substitution. Preserve all other source instructions and exact protocol tokens.
